Hi Alex — quick technical follow-up covering the points you raised. TL;DR: session affinity can be supported in active-active with a few tradeoffs; fallback model quality can be benchmarked against your prompts.

1) Session affinity + active-active
- We support sticky routing (per-session affinity) at the edge while still running active-active inference clusters in multiple regions. The sticky layer directs a session to a preferred region for KV/cache locality; if that region is unreachable, the request fails over to the nearest region and we proxy the KV cache (with a brief cold miss).
- Tradeoffs: active-active with strong cache locality requires very low replication lag or a strategy that tolerates eventual consistency for non-critical KV entries. For your p95 targets, sticky + local KV cache should meet the numbers given normal network conditions; under multi-region failover you’ll see a temporary p95 spike that our fallback policies smooth.

2) Quantized fallback and quality
- We maintain performance/quality profiles for each quantized variant. If you share a small prompt set (5–10 representative prompts), we’ll run an A/B regression and provide delta metrics (perplexity, token-level ROUGE for structured outputs, and human-evaluated spot checks).

3) Throughput estimates / concurrency
- Based on your stated 50–75 steady concurrent users and expected peaks ~150, we recommend reserving ~2–3 inference slots per concurrent session for streaming workloads (to preserve low per-token latency). Ballpark throughput: ~200–400 QPS regional peak depending on prompt size and streaming overhead. Exact numbers in the attached routing diagram.

4) Data residency & logging
- EU-region data residency supported: requests originating from EU will be served from EU clusters; audit logs for EU tenants can be stored in EU KMS-backed buckets. We can provide export controls language and encryption key handling in the contract pack.

See attached: regional-routing-diagram.png (high-level topology + estimated p95 numbers per region). I’ll follow up with a short doc showing active-active vs affinity cost delta.
